skill.name: hyperframes-cli
skill.description: Guides the HyperFrames CLI workflow for scaffolding, validation, Studio preview, local video rendering, diagnostics, asset preparation, publishing, and AWS Lambda rendering.
skill.summary: Operate HyperFrames projects from setup through validated local or cloud rendering.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, public examples, and expected project paths. Confirmed concerns include host fingerprinting, forced remote skill updates, unpinned command execution, automatic feedback transmission, and arbitrary URL capture. Publication should require explicit consent, pinned dependencies, and network destination controls.

remediation.suggestion: Pin HyperFrames to a reviewed version and integrity hash. Inspect project wrappers and require user confirmation before first execution.
Honor --skip-skills. Require opt-in updates, pin GitHub commits, verify hashes, and show changes before replacing global skills.
Block loopback, link-local, private, and cloud metadata destinations by default. Revalidate every redirect and require approval for non-public targets.
Ask before sending feedback or environment metadata. Display the destination and payload, minimize fields, and preserve a persistent opt-out.

semantic_findings.title: Forced remote skill updates
semantic_findings.description: Every init checks GitHub and replaces global skills, while the documented --skip-skills flag is ignored. A compromised upstream can change future agent instructions without approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The behavior is stated directly in both the main workflow and the scaffolding reference.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned command and wrapper execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill runs npx hyperframes without a version pin and says to obey a project-local wrapper exactly. Mutable packages or repository-controlled wrappers can execute changed code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The execution guidance is explicit, but external package or repository controls may provide protections not shown here.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic feedback sends environment metadata
semantic_findings.description: After successful renders, the agent is directed to submit ratings and comments automatically. The payload includes operating system, Node, CPU, memory, and FFmpeg details.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill mandates feedback after rendering, and the reference explicitly lists the attached environment summary.

semantic_findings.title: Telemetry fingerprints sandbox and agent runtimes
semantic_findings.description: Telemetry classifies sandbox and agent runtimes from pseudo-files and environment-variable existence. This reveals execution context even though values and direct PII are excluded.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The telemetry fields, detection sources, and opt-out controls are explicitly documented.

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary URL capture lacks documented destination controls
semantic_findings.description: Capture accepts a supplied URL, loads the page, and downloads assets without documented destination restrictions. Internal URLs could expose services or cloud metadata to the CLI.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Arbitrary URL loading is explicit, but the CLI implementation may contain protections not shown in these documentation files.

content.value_statement: HyperFrames projects require many CLI commands and validation steps. This skill guides scaffolding, diagnostics, preview, local rendering, and AWS Lambda rendering.
actual_capabilities: Scaffold editable projects from templates, local media, or live URLs with HyperFrames init and capture.
Run static linting, runtime validation, layout inspection, motion checks, comparisons, and snapshots.
Start Studio previews and retrieve compact context for the user-selected element.
Render local video formats with quality, resolution, strict validation, and variable overrides.
Diagnose Node.js, FFmpeg, Chrome, Docker, memory, disk, and browser installation issues.
Deploy and manage AWS Lambda rendering stacks, site uploads, progress, IAM policies, and cleanup.
limitations: Local workflows require Node.js 22 or later and FFmpeg.
AWS Lambda rendering also requires AWS credentials, AWS SAM CLI, Bun, permissions, and cloud spending.
The skill guides CLI operations but relies on other HyperFrames skills for detailed composition design.
Some commands download packages or models, upload project files, or contact telemetry services.

use_cases.title: Create an editable product video
use_cases.description: Scaffold a project, validate the composition, review it in Studio, and render an approved delivery file.

use_cases.title: Add rendering checks to CI
use_cases.description: Run machine-readable lint, validation, inspection, snapshots, and strict rendering gates on a build runner.

use_cases.title: Scale long renders in AWS
use_cases.description: Prepare IAM permissions, deploy the Lambda stack, upload a site, monitor progress, and clean up resources.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold a project
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a HyperFrames project named [name] with the [template] example at [resolution]. Check prerequisites and stop before previewing.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a composition
prompt_templates.prompt: In [project path], run lint, validate, inspect, and meaningful snapshots. Fix confirmed defects, summarize changes, and rerun every check.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an approved render
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [project path] in HyperFrames Studio on an available port. Report the project URL, wait for approval, then render [format] at [quality].

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Lambda render
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess local versus AWS Lambda rendering for [project path] and [workload]. Check prerequisites, validate IAM, estimate steps, and require approval before deployment.

output_examples.input: Check why preview fails on a fresh CI runner.
output: Node.js is below the required version.
FFmpeg is unavailable on the runner.
Studio preview was not started because prerequisites failed.

output_examples.input: Validate my motion-heavy launch video before review.
output: Layout and motion checks found two blocking issues.
Snapshots were captured at meaningful scene timestamps for review.

output_examples.input: Prepare a 4K Lambda render for a long project.
output_examples.output: The plan recommends Lambda, lists missing AWS prerequisites, explains supersampling, and waits for approval before deployment or upload.

best_practices: Run lint, validate, inspect, and targeted snapshots before opening Studio or rendering.
Use machine-readable output in CI, but evaluate documented payload fields instead of assuming exit codes are sufficient.
Require user approval before rendering, publishing, cloud deployment, feedback submission, or public issue sharing.
anti_patterns: Do not render immediately after checks without Studio review and user approval.
Do not place secrets in command arguments, feedback comments, published projects, or committed state files.
Do not use unreviewed wrappers, mutable package versions, or arbitrary internal capture URLs.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages HyperFrames CLI setup, validation, preview, rendering, diagnostics, publishing, asset commands, and AWS Lambda workflows.

faq.question: Does it design the video composition?
faq.answer: It can guide the workflow, but detailed HTML composition, animation, registry, and media decisions use related HyperFrames skills.

faq.question: What software is required locally?
faq.answer: Local work requires Node.js 22 or later and FFmpeg. Browser, Docker, and GPU requirements depend on the chosen command.

faq.question: Can it render without user approval?
faq.answer: The documented workflow requires Studio review and explicit approval before rendering.

faq.question: Does it use network or cloud services?
faq.answer: Yes. Capture, updates, publishing, telemetry, feedback, model downloads, npm access, and AWS Lambda can contact external services.

faq.question: How should sensitive projects be handled?
faq.answer: Review outbound commands, disable telemetry, avoid public publishing, protect AWS state, restrict capture destinations, and confirm every upload.
